title: United Bankshares and the University of Georgia Athletic Association are Proud to Announce the Winner of the 2026 Arch Award
summary: ATLANTA and ATHENS, GA—For the sixth consecutive year, the University of Georgia Athletic Association and United Bankshares are recognizing former athletes who have transitioned from the field of play to become leaders in the world of business. body_markdown:
**ATLANTA and ATHENS, GA** – For the sixth consecutive year, the University of Georgia Athletic Association and United Bankshares are recognizing former athletes who have transitioned from the field of play to become leaders in the world of business. Former UGA volleyball and basketball player Maria Taylor (’09) is this year's Arch Award recipient, joining a host of former UGA athletes honored in past years.


“The dedication, discipline, and leadership required to succeed as a student-athlete are the same qualities that drive success in the professional world. Through this award, we are proud to recognize former student-athletes who have built outstanding careers and continue to make meaningful contributions to their industries and communities,” said Monty Watson, Regional President, United Bankshares. “Their achievements demonstrate that the lessons learned through athletics extend far beyond the field and provide a strong foundation for lifelong success.”


The 2026 Arch Award recipient was recognized on Dooley Field at Sanford Stadium during the November 14 game against Missouri.


A born-and-raised Georgian, Maria Taylor earned a degree in broadcast news from the University of Georgia in 2009 and later earned her MBA from UGA in 2013. As a student-athlete, she competed in both volleyball and basketball, earning three All-SEC volleyball selections and being named to the USA A2 National Volleyball Team. After graduating, Taylor launched a successful broadcasting career at ESPN, where she has served as a host, analyst, and reporter for the biggest events in college football and basketball. In 2017, she became the first Black woman to co-host ESPN's College GameDay. Throughout her career, she has covered the College Football Playoff National Championship, SEC Nation, ABC Saturday Night Football, and the NCAA Women's Final Four.


Beyond broadcasting, Taylor co-founded the Winning Edge Leadership Academy in 2015, a nonprofit that mentors and supports women and minority students pursuing careers in the sports industry. Since its founding, the academy has helped more than 40 students. Through her professional accomplishments and commitment to developing future leaders, Taylor continues to have a lasting impact on sports media and her community.


“Maria Taylor represents the very best of the University of Georgia,” J. Reid Parker Director of Athletics Josh Brooks said. “As a distinguished alumni, she has built an ultra-successful career and serves as one of our university’s greatest ambassadors. There is no one more deserving of the Arch Award than Maria.” To learn more about previous winners of the Arch Award Presented by United Bankshares and their success on and off the field, please visit[here](https://static.georgiadogs.com/custompages/other/Arch-Award/?sidearmRedirect=true) .


**About United Bankshares**


United Bankshares is a premier regional bank and a subsidiary of United Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: UBSI). United has consolidated assets of approximately $34 billion with over 240 offices located across Virginia, Washington, D.C., Maryland, West Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. The Bank is dedicated to growing the relationships it has built since 1839 and offering a competitive suite of banking and lending products, treasury management, wealth management, mortgage services, personal and business credit cards, and more. United Bank operates under the DBA United Bankshares in the state of Georgia.[Learn more](https://www.bankwithunited.com/about-united.html) about United Bankshares.
